title: Surjectivity of a quotient killing all adjoin generators
statement: Let $R$ and $K$ be commutative rings, with an $R$-algebra structure on $K$, let $s$ be a subset of $K$, and put $S=R[s]$. If $q$ is an ideal of $S$ containing every element of $s$, then the algebra map $R \to S/q$ is surjective.

source.place: Tag 0334, Step 5, surjectivity in the quotient presentation R[x]/xR[x] = R/J; elementary generalization to an arbitrary generating set.

proof.text: Lift a quotient class to S. Induct on its adjoin membership: a generator maps to zero, constants lift to themselves, and sums and products lift using the corresponding operations on constants. This proves surjectivity. The argument includes the empty generating set and the zero quotient.

proof_origin.place: Generalization of the existing singleton quotient-map proof by adjoin induction, shared by both callers to remove duplicate private proofs.
